subject: Renewal amendment: add reserved GPUs for long-context model + reranker
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal amendment: add reserved GPUs for long-context model + reranker

Hi Alex —

As we discussed on Friday, I attached a brief proposal that folds the extra capacity you asked for into the upcoming renewal. High-level changes we recommend:

- Add a dedicated reserved pool of 12 GPUs (H100) for production workloads, configurable as two 6-GPU pools for staging + prod.
- Add 8 burst GPUs (pay-as-you-go) for periodic retraining/large-batch jobs.
- Support the new model mix: move one service to our 70B-equivalent long-context model (64k tokens). Expect ~1.8x GPU utilization vs the current 32k model.
- Add the Reranker add-on (search/QA pipeline) as an optional line item — estimated extra 3 GPUs for throughput at 99th percentile SLA.
- Throughput guarantee: baseline 500 requests/min with 95th percentile latency SLA 350ms for generation endpoints (configurable).
- Term: 12-month commit (option for 24 months with additional 12% discount).

Attached: renewal_capacity_proposal_acme_v2.pdf (summary + cost), SOW_acme_dedicated_addendum.xlsx (SOW draft), perf_summary_long_context.csv (benchmarks).

Next steps: can you confirm acceptance of the pool sizing and whether you want the reranker as part of the committed scope or as an add-on? If this looks good, Rishi will circulate an updated quote and DocuSign for signature.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal amendment: add reserved GPUs for long-context model + reranker

Jasmine —

Thanks for the write-up and attachments. A few quick clarifications from our infra and security teams: 

1) The 64k context model sounds right for the new clinical summarization flow, but do you have concrete perf numbers vs our current 32k model for median and p99? Attached perf_summary_long_context.csv has a lot, but our infra team wants a TL;DR.
2) Will the reranker be colocated in the same reserved pool or run in a separate pool with its own throughput SLA?
3) For compliance, we need SOC 2 evidence and an uplift on audit logging retention (currently 90 days) to 365 days. Is that doable as part of the dedicated offering?

We prefer to keep the reranker as a committed line item if pricing is competitive — reduces ops for our team. Also, if we go to 24 months, we'd need better price protection on token costs (cap increases).

Happy to jump on a quick call this week to walk through the perf numbers.

—Alex
VP Product, Platform
Acme Health Systems
alex.kim@acmehealth.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@acmehealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal amendment: add reserved GPUs for long-context model + reranker

Alex —

Quick perf TL;DR based on the bench runs included in perf_summary_long_context.csv and our internal 70B-equivalent profile: 

- Median token latency (gen-only, batch size 1): 18ms/token on H100 (fp16 baseline).
- 95th percentile: 42ms/token with KV cache warm.
- For 64k context runs, peak memory pressure increases ~70% vs 32k; effective throughput per GPU drops ~1.7x depending on request mix.
- Reranker microservice (rerank top-10) averages 45ms per request when using our optimized fused kernels; plan for ~3 GPUs with continuous throughput target of 600 QPS to meet 99th percentile latency target.

Recommendations:
- Use H100 for the long-context pool (memory + tensor perf advantages).
- Enable 4-bit quantization for the majority of the pipeline to reduce GPU memory by ~30% while keeping quality delta <1% on our evals.
- Put the reranker in a logically separate reserved pool (3 GPUs) but allow burst to the main pool for degraded scenarios. This preserves isolation for latencies.

I can run a short validation cluster next week against a small prompt set you provide — will need a 2-hour window.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@acmehealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal amendment: add reserved GPUs for long-context model + reranker

Alex —

Thanks for the quick review. Based on the inputs here, I've drafted an amendment and quote reflecting: 

- Committed: 12x H100 reserved (two 6-GPU pools: prod/staging), 3x H100 reserved for reranker, 8x H100 burst (pay-as-you-go).
- Monthly recurring: $122,400 / month (pre-discount) for committed capacity.
- One-time SOW for migration & validation: $42,500.
- 12-month term: standard pricing. 24-month term: 12% contract-level discount on committed monthly.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for dedicated pools; latency SLOs as described in the SOW. Credits: prorated credits up to 10% of monthly committed fees for missed SLA on uptime.

I dropped in a DocuSign link to the quote + the SOW. If you want the reranker as a committed item, I included it; if you prefer to treat it as add-on we can mark it optional and reduce the committed monthly accordingly.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/1234-ACME-RENEWAL
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/deal/RDW-ACME-2026-R1

If this looks good, please sign the DocuSign and we'll schedule the validation run (Lauren will lead). Happy to hop on a call.

—Rishi

- Increase audit log retention to 365 days (we can accept a small monthly add-on).
- Can you provide a 60-day price protection window on token unit costs if we sign for 24 months?

If we get those concessions, I can get this to our CFO/legal for sign-off by EOW. Also, will need SOC 2 Type II snapshot for last 12 months attached to the DocuSign envelope.

—Alex
